title: Managed TURN credentials authorize private-network peer permissions
description: Native relay HEAD be6222991e6b0d3c7a5de92e0ebe05666683e6d8 generated no private-peer ACL. The bundled coturn accepted CREATE_PERMISSION for RFC1918 and CGNAT addresses under a synthetic valid TURN credential. The same absent rules existed in the root Docker entrypoint; its generated patched configuration was checked with the native helper, not the Linux image. The Docker source baseline is root HEAD d70558f9e1b88c20359c45cd13c1484e8c8a6406.
root_cause: TURN authentication was present, but the managed call transport configuration did not limit peer destination address ranges. Credential holders could obtain permissions for addresses on the operator LAN.
intended_behavior: Credentials for public call transport must not grant permissions to relay toward private, loopback, link-local or special-purpose address space. Intentional private-network TURN deployments require explicit external operator configuration.

trace.description: Generates authenticated TURN config without destination deny rules.
Passes the generated file to the bundled coturn process. The test exercised its native CREATE_PERMISSION protocol.

evidence.description: Baseline native policy accepted 10.0.0.1,172.16.0.1,192.168.0.1,100.64.0.1. Link-local was already denied by helper defaults.
Patched native and Docker-generated policies reject RFC1918/CGNAT/link-local, IPv6 loopback/ULA/link-local and IPv4-mapped10/8; global IPv4/IPv6 controls succeed.
Reproducible loopback-only native helper probe; creates permissions but sends no peer traffic.

Related Docker entrypoint at root d70558f9e1b88c20359c45cd13c1484e8c8a6406 independently omitted destination denies; patched rendered policy was tested with the bundled macOS helper, not the Linux image.

conditions.description: Attacker holds a valid, nonexpired TURN credential.
Managed TURN is running with the generated configuration.
Reaching an actual private service would additionally require the operator host to route to that service. This was not tested.

execution.attacker_perspective: Use an issued TURN credential to request private peer permissions.
payloads: Authenticated STUN CREATE_PERMISSION requests for 10.0.0.1,172.16.0.1,192.168.0.1 and 100.64.0.1.
Patched negative checks also include 169.254.169.254,::1,::ffff:10.0.0.1,fc00::1 and fe80::1; positive controls 1.1.1.1 and 2001:4860:4860::8888.
instructions: Run python3 Scripts/test_managed_coturn_peer_policy.py on macOS with Xcode. It compiles actual native configuration, copies and ad-hoc signs only a disposable helper copy, and binds listeners to 127.0.0.1/::1.
For original behavior, run the preserved turn-permission-probe.py baseline.conf in the ignored evidence directory.
The script sends ALLOCATE and CREATE_PERMISSION messages only; it never issues SEND, CHANNEL_BIND, or a connection to a peer address.
execution.observed_result: Baseline private permissions returned success 0x108. Patched restricted permissions return 403; global IPv4 and IPv6 controls return success. Both native and actual Docker-entrypoint-generated configurations pass against the bundled macOS helper. No private target responses or Linux container runtime behavior was tested.

remediation.strategy: Add explicit private/special destination deny ranges to native and Docker managed TURN configurations. Document private-network deployment as an explicit external service. Docker now creates its private config using exclusive mktemp rather than predictable redirection.

likelihood.reason: Requires a valid TURN credential and a reachable managed TURN instance.

impact.reason: Private-peer authorization enables unintended network reachability conditional on host routing; bounded test proved permission acceptance, not private-service response or data compromise.

confidence.reason: Real bundled helper protocol responses establish the policy gap and fix, including IPv4-mapped IPv6 and positive controls. Linux image runtime remains outside validated coverage.
